title: 10 Best Triosteum Perfoliatum Preparations

Teas and decoctions are commonly used to harness its anti-inflammatory and soothing properties. Tinctures provide a concentrated form for more potent effects. Mucillages, derived from the plant's gelatinous components, are used to coat and protect the digestive tract. Poultices, made by crushing the fresh herb, are applied topically to reduce swelling and promote healing.
